definitions.meaning: a set of drinks bought for everyone in a group at the pub
two slices of bread with a filling count as one of these

explanation.definitionFit: Both a pub order of drinks for the whole table and a single made-up sandwich go by this word.

clue.text: Proper period in which data may be processed

definitions.text: Proper period in which data may be processed

parts.note: proper means genuine or real
a period is a stretch of time

explanation.surface: A description of the moment a computer handles its data.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and its first two words also build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Computing that happens instantly, as events occur, is said to be done in this way.

clue.text: Lined up awkwardly, not in stacks

indicators.note: done awkwardly means arranged clumsily, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Things placed in a clumsy row rather than heaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges the letters of LINED UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not heaped into piles has not been stacked up.

indicators.note: the word first asks for the opening letter of the word dog's

parts.note: Noah's ark was a vessel that saved lives in the Flood

explanation.surface: A dark-coated dog takes its place on a lifeboat first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' picks D from dog's.
explanation.definitionFit: Black and this word both describe the absence of light.

parts.note: like means in the same way as, giving AS
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A phonetics lesson on sounding the H in the name Hook.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Hook is the pirate villain of Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics, to breathe out an h sound at the start of a word is to do this.

clue.text: I ostracise Lucy for switching to state benefits

indicators.note: switching letters around means rearranging them, so these words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone shuns Lucy for moving onto welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching' rearranges the fourteen letters of I OSTRACISE LUCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare payments from the government are known collectively by this name.

clue.text: Carl leaves city for place across the water

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the name Carl is taken away from the city

parts.note: Carlisle is a city in Cumbria, in north-west England
taken as written

explanation.surface: Carl quits the city and heads for somewhere overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes CARL from CARLISLE, a city in northern England near the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a piece of land one reaches by crossing the sea.

definitions.meaning: pure and lovely, as a child's face may be
Gabriel is an archangel, so like him means heavenly in nature

explanation.definitionFit: Saintly sweetness, and resembling a heavenly messenger such as Gabriel, are both covered by this adjective.

clue.text: Three points taken by my opponent

parts.note: E, N and E are three compass points
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rival scores three points to win.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'points' are compass points, not scores: East, North, East.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversary or foe is someone set against you.

clue.text: Tried many things, having competed on pitch

definitions.meaning: sampled lots of options, especially romantic partners, rather than committing
taken part as a fielder or player in a game outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for dabbling widely instead of settling down literally means having taken part out on the sports ground.

clue.text: Corps appears in shock old clothing

indicators.note: appears in means shows up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to shock someone is to appal them
RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps

explanation.surface: Something about a military unit dressed in startling vintage outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corps' looks like part of the surface's soldiers, but it is the Royal Engineers, signalled by 'appears in'; 'old' belongs to the definition, since the word now sounds formal or dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are an old-fashioned or formal sense of the word, as in fine attire.

clue.text: Perfume from pine product has something woody in it

indicators.note: in it means placed inside the previous item, so one word sits within another

parts.note: a pine tree produces cones
a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A fragrance made from pine with a woody note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in it' signals the container; 'pine product' looks like resin or oil but is the fruiting body of the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de Cologne is a light scented water, a kind of fragrance.

definitions.meaning: to work the soil, ploughing it ready for crops
the cash drawer in a shop counter

explanation.definitionFit: Ploughing farmland and a shop's cash register share this four-letter word.

indicators.note: wrong means mistaken, so the letters of lady are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Thomas gave a woman the wrong name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges LADY. The poet is Dylan Thomas, so the surname is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh poet Thomas had this as his first name.

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the next

parts.note: surreptitious means sneaky or sly

explanation.surface: Someone sneaky goes about committing a murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps SLY around A.
explanation.definitionFit: To murder or put to death violently is the sense here.

parts.note: a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: Lavish compliments for a well-behaved pet parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: A lory is a parrot of Australasia.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown and high honour, as in glory to God, is great praise.

parts.note: a comic is a magazine, informally a mag
US means American

explanation.surface: A cartoon sorcerer from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' is a noun here, a mag, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a sorcerer or magician, like the Magi of old.

clue.text: I'd get backed in centre position in 1500m race

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the turned letters go into the other phrase

parts.note: the centre is the middle
a stance is a position or posture

indicators.note: get backed means go backwards, so the letters of I'd are reversed

explanation.surface: Instructions for an athlete's position in a 1500m race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get backed' reverses I'D and 'in' signals the container; the 1500 metres is the classic race of this category in athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: Track races of 800 to 1500 metres are classed between sprints and long-distance events.

clue.text: The college to give you a flying start?

definitions.text: The college to give you a flying start?

parts.words: The college to give you a flying start?
parts.note: a flying start sounds like getting off to a good beginning, but here means being trained to fly as an RAF officer

explanation.surface: A college that sets its students off to a strong beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: Cranwell in Lincolnshire is the Royal Air Force's officer training college.
explanation.definitionFit: The RAF College in Lincolnshire trains officers who will fly.

parts.note: honest in the idiom, but read literally as over a shop's counter-top, where goods are sold without a prescription

explanation.surface: A query about whether something is honest.
explanation.walkthrough: Medicines sold without a prescription are sold this way; a counter is a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-the-counter goods are sold openly across a shop's board-like counter.

indicators.note: a helping is a portion, so only part of the words loves persons is taken

explanation.surface: Lovers help out at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' takes a portion of LOVES PERSONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong, the evening prayer service, is also called by this name.

parts.note: anyway, at the end of a sentence, means the same as though

explanation.surface: Anyway, it is time to stop and reflect.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemplation or careful thinking is meant here.

clue.text: About to request a barrel of beer

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: About to order a keg of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa, 'about') is used with dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden barrel for holding ale is this sort of container.

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: Searching an old valley from end to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts COMB round O. A coomb is a short valley, often in a chalk hillside in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb, also spelled combe, is a small steep-sided valley.

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction meaning loudly or strongly
ire is anger or indignation

explanation.surface: Someone fiercely and righteously angry.
explanation.walkthrough: F stands for forte, Italian for loud or strong in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire or ablaze is burning.

clue.text: Horse raced, to come in first in Oaks

indicators.note: to come in means to enter, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: raced means ran

indicators.note: first in asks for the opening letter of the word Oaks

explanation.surface: A horse ran and won the Oaks race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first in' picks O from Oaks; 'to come in' puts it inside RAN. The Oaks is an English classic flat race for fillies.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat mixes white with another colour.

indicators.note: invests means puts into, so the money letter goes inside the youth word

parts.note: a cub is a youngster, as in a cub reporter or Cub Scout
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A society putting money into young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invests' puts L (pound) inside CUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is an association of people with shared interests.

clue.text: Refuse seat on plane-that's a jolt

definitions.meaning: an airline turning away a passenger from an overbooked flight
a sudden knock or jarring movement

explanation.definitionFit: Airlines use this word for denying a booked passenger a seat, and it also means a jarring knock.

parts.note: over means about, as in a row over money
a fib is a lie

explanation.surface: Someone takes the high ground about a small untruth.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie on top of something is to take the upper position.

clue.text: Get huge problems in Indian ritual murder

indicators.note: problems suggests things going wrong, so the letters of get huge are scrambled

explanation.surface: A great deal of trouble in a historic Indian killing cult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problems' rearranges GET HUGE. The Thugs were a historical Indian gang of ritual stranglers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thugs of India practised robbery and murder by strangling, and their practice was called this.

parts.note: active means busy
a body is a group of people, a team

explanation.surface: An interfering person signs up to a lively team.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosy interferer in others' affairs is the meaning.

clue.text: Penny delayed returning with a bit of bloom

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for delayed is read backwards

parts.note: delayed means late

explanation.surface: Penny is late coming back with a piece of a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns LATE into ETAL.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the coloured leaves of a flower head is part of a blossom.
